claims_and_derivations.claim: In the strong-coupling adiabatic model for an axially symmetric shape rotor, the coordinate about the symmetry axis (3-axis) is redundant, expressed by constraint R_3 = 0 (no collective mass rotation about shape symmetry axis). This does not imply that for any arbitrary microscopic axially symmetric many-body system the cranking response or effective inertia about the symmetry axis must be zero. For physical core angular momentum R_perp = hbar (mathcalI_perp - j_perp) and dimensionless I, K, j, collective Hamiltonian is H_coll = R_perp^2 / (2 J_perp) = hbar^2 (mathcalI_perp - j_perp)^2 / (2 J_perp). Neglecting off-diagonal Coriolis mixing and absorbing constant terms gives E_K(I) - E_intr = hbar^2 [I(I+1) - K^2] / (2 J_perp) for I >= K. Bandhead spin I_bandhead = K holds in this model under allowed signature/parity conditions; observed bandhead can differ in real nuclei.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Small-amplitude wobbling phonon tagging requires localization in the quadratic expansion basin where higher-order terms are small. It does not require all three inertias to be distinct (high-K axisymmetric limit has local expansion). Quasiparticle parameter evolution along a spin sequence must be distinguished from time evolution; coupled RPA modes can remain harmonic (as in Section 3.6). Competing mechanisms for companion bands with smoothly varying Delta E(I) include: signature partner bands (alpha = +- 1/2), quasiparticle configuration crossings, and dynamic coupling to a gamma-soft core. Level energies plus relative branching ratios alone do not yield absolute B; when lacking lifetime and CoulEx/absolute RME data, absolute transition strengths cannot be independently determined. Explicitgamma-softIBFM andfixed-gammaunfrozenQTR aredistinct implementations, not identical collectivefreedom.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Multi-dimensional spectroscopic criteria: (1) DCO ratio R_DCO(delta) is a rational function of two quadratics; solving it yields two real roots, a degenerate root, or no real root (excluding poles where denominator vanishes). Linear polarization P provides complementary electric/magnetic character, not direct level parity; same-event DCO/P are not statistically independent. (2) delta(E2/M1) is defined with photon wave number k = E_gamma/(hbar c) paired with charge-type magnetic operator M_S(M1) = M_mu/c (units e fm), or M_mu with E_gamma/hbar, without extra c^2. (3) 1/I is an asymptotic large-I limit with fixed parameters; M1 strength is not universally quenched (Frauendorf 2014 QTR has M1 limitations). (4) Judgment can rely on effective phenomenological models (IBFM, PRM) as well as microscopic frameworks.
